prompt: A clean scientific forest plot summarising four randomised trials of a post-operative painkiller, effect measured as pain-score reduction in points. The four studies, their effect estimates, standard errors and fixed-effect weights are: Aldana 2019, estimate 3.47, SE 0.62, weight 25%; Bellucci 2020, estimate 1.92, SE 0.41, weight 30%; Csorba 2021, estimate 4.08, SE 0.87, weight 15%; Duarte 2023, estimate 2.61, SE 0.55, weight 30%. Each study row shows a square marker at its estimate with a horizontal 95% confidence-interval line, and in a right-hand text column the entry 'estimate [lower, upper]' where lower and upper are the 95% CI bounds computed as the estimate minus and plus 1.96 times that study's SE, rounded to two decimals (round halves up). Below the four rows, a filled pooled diamond centred at the fixed-effect pooled estimate, computed as the weighted average of the four estimates using the weights given, rounded to two decimals; print that pooled value in the text column of the pooled row (no CI for the pooled row). Also print each study's label and weight on its row. No other numbers except a simple 0-6 axis scale. White background.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a meta-analysis forest plot with study rows, confidence-interval lines and a pooled diamond? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
